title: BYD Electric Vehicles added to Origin EV Power Up - Charge at 8¢/kWh @ Origin Energy
body:
Deal: BYD Electric Vehicles added to Origin EV Power Up - Charge at 8¢/kWh @ Origin Energy

[belongsinforums] They don't list any times. Agl guarantees 12-6 every night.
[tanksinatra] That's the whole point, it's based on grid demand not fixed times. I generally got about 5-8 hours of charging in the evening with the plan.
[belongsinforums] How does it turn on? I suppose this is only possible with a wall charger as a granny charger is dumb
[belongsinforums] @tanksinatra: To the car? When it's off?
[tanksinatra] @belongsinforums: Yep. Implementation varies by car, but that's pretty much it.
[Nom] Can you override it when you need to ? If you have a long journey coming up, it would be pretty 💩 to find your car had only charged to 70% last night !
[11112007] Depends on whether you need the full 100% - if you do then you override or set a command that forces the full charge.
I've had an EV for around 10 years - i barely do 350km a week so even with an installed 32A charger i let it trickle charge (10A) off my house battery most nights i have it plugged it.
[Hellfire] Mine has always charged to 100% overnight (or whatever I set the limit to).
[enigma48] Yep. The “instant charge at full rate” button means they don’t throttle. But then you pay full price.
[Hellfire] Mine tends to start charging around 11pm and continues past 7am. It will also charge during the day if you leave it plugged in, maybe a few hours.
[carrawa] Just check if you ordered a BYD 2026 model and got a 2025 model.
[Loracks] Is this some kind of VPP arrangement with certain EVs? So you never know when it might be charging at that cost?
Seems easier to have a set time (12-6) and just have the car on scheduled charging. Cheaper too at around 4c
[winaxter] It works by origin controlling when your car charges. So you leave your car plugged in, and when there is low usage from the power grid, origin will automatically start charging your car. When there is high usage and electricity costs are high, it will stop charging. Had both, and generally just prefer the ease of 12-6 cheap charging.
[derdew] is all the power used in the house charged at that rate in those times, or just the ev's use?
[GregFiona] Powershop is midnight to 6am , 4.99c/kWh for all EVs and you can charge your home battery etc at the same time
[derdew] yes I know. I'm with ovo, so prefer clear time periods. but just wondering if this particular plan covers all use?
[BatmanAU] I spoke with Origin about this, and they were um and ahh not sure Sir. AGL were just as bad with rates and times, if not worse.
[tesla] For this reason I stay with AGL which does not impose any particular brand / model.
[noise36] In Perth we can use power for anything at that price every day between 9am and 3pm on the EV plan.
[Switchblade88] Could you not just… lie?
EV plugs don't transmit vehicle data in any form over a charging cable. The charger only gets the vehicles' maximum charging rate, which is a basic 1kHz PWM signal which is not brand-dependent. Nothing will stop you using a different branded EV, Origin literally can't check.
[DOGGYWOWWOW] That's why they use the internet connected car to control charging
[BatmanAU] Apparently it links to your app, which obviously has the car information in it. Nothing to say you couldnt use a friends app to login too… maybe
[Switchblade88] So they're relying on vehicle demand control rather than charger supply control? That would makes sense, I suppose, but it looks to require an ungodly amount of hoops to jump through to get it to work.
I'm guessing it's Origin -> your phone app -> BYD cloud -> your car, which seems more convoluted than Origin -> your EV charger
And if you're plugged in elsewhere then you still have Origin controlling your charging, despite not being home with your own power? Or do you give them location permission as well?
The rates aren't good enough to justify these hurdles IMO
[BatmanAU] Yeah im not sure to be honest (especially BYD), but its an Origin app, same as the Watchla Tesla app, it would read your data through allowing permission and starting the charging as if you were using the BYD/Tesla app to charge from another location. If thats the case, then yes the origin app would get your car data, VIN etc.
But i agree, jump on the OVO or AGL 12 to 6, same rates. You might even find that these have cheaper daily supply charges etc too, plus some are offering $200 join up credit
[BatmanAU] You could go the OVO energy FREE 3 plan if you dont require a full battery. This gives you 3 hours of free energy plus another 2 hours at $0.06 per kWh for another 2 hours on off peak time per day.
[apaul] we have been with AGL's 12-6 8c plan is for a while . I charge my home battery and EV . also run the high wattage equipment's during the same time (diswasher , dryer etc)..
[Maxdax] Ex Origin customer
By far I feel Origin has the best customer retention policy of any utility provider - the offer may or may NOT be great but they without fail call me every Six months to come back to Origin ( I had left them 18month back )
Im on TOU - Ausgrid - Their latest offer was a standard peak rate of 0.33 & off peak of 0.8 (12 to 6am) - daily charge was around .90 with $200 cash back after 90 days
My AGL EV plan works out ONLY slightly cheaper but I’m considering it for the $200 cash back
They said it’s NOT advertised YET - & only a retention offer for EV customers
No vehicle demand control
